newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Wednesday on short-covering by retail investors, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 3,189 yuan ($384) per tonne, rising nine yuan. It opened at an intraday low of 3,180 and hit a high of 3,190 yuan per tonne.
November rose two to 3,168 yuan per tonne, the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 3,152 and March put on three to 3,148 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 23,700 tonnes from 23,500 tonnes.
Soybeans opened mostly higher and moved around opening levels for most of the session, traders said.
"Short-covering by retail investors dominated today's trading, but most institutional investors stayed on the sidelines due to a lack of market-moving news," one trader said.
Hot money continued to flow out of the soybean market, traders said, adding they expected soybeans to move in a narrow range in coming days.
